statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-41907 is patched in uuid 11.1.1. Trigger.dev's lockfile still resolves uuid 3.x/8.x/9.x/10.x for legacy transitive consumers; forcing those majors to 11.x breaks API compatibility. The webapp's uuid@^11 consumers already receive 11.1.1+ via pnpm overrides. Assessing reachability and upstream migration for the remaining legacy uuid resolutions.

The missing buffer bounds check (GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq) only triggers when a caller passes an output buffer to uuid v3/v5/v6. Uptime Kuma generates random v4 UUIDs and does not invoke the v3/v5/v6 buffer APIs, so the vulnerable path is not exercised by the application. The first fixed release (11.1.1) is a major version bump from the 8.x/10.x copies still resolved transitively (via hyperid and dockerode), which carries breaking-change risk that is being evaluated. Reachability proof and a non-breaking remediation are under assessment.

uuid@9.0.1 is vulnerable to CVE-2026-41907 (MEDIUM severity, silent partial writes into caller-provided buffers in v3/v5/v6 functions). The fix is available in uuid@11.1.1. However, upgrading from uuid@9.x to uuid@11.x is a major version jump that would require significant testing and may introduce breaking changes in transitive dependencies. The vulnerability affects applications that pass external buffers to uuid v3/v5/v6 functions with attacker-controlled offsets or undersized buffers; langfuse's typical usage does not expose this attack surface.

uuid@11.1.0 is vulnerable to CVE-2026-41907 (MEDIUM severity, silent partial writes into caller-provided buffers in v3/v5/v6 functions). The fix is available in uuid@11.1.1. However, upgrading is blocked because oci-common@2.127.0 (a transitive dependency) deep-imports uuid/v1, which was removed in uuid@11.x. Upgrading uuid would break oci-common at runtime. A fix requires either an oci-common update that removes the uuid/v1 deep-import or a workaround that maintains compatibility. The vulnerability affects applications that pass external buffers to uuid v3/v5/v6 functions with attacker-controlled offsets or undersized buffers; langfuse's typical usage does not expose this attack surface.
